answer: A mechanism that actually bites: cap per-account emission and put the surplus into a pool earned only by non-duplicate work, because oasis only stays cheap while duplicating content caps out because the pool rewards novelty, not volume. Concretely, lotus is enforced in the ledger: Nothing here needs to be perfect; it only has to make clones cost more than they return. Any timber approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. That converts sybil attacks from an economic play into a pure loss.
